topic: reddit shifts to logged-in experience amid declining search traffic
headline_marked: Reddit [[shifts to logged-in experience]] to combat AI scraping and declining search traffic
headline: Reddit shifts to logged-in experience to combat AI scraping and declining search traffic
summary: The social media giant is making a significant change to its platform, aiming to protect its data and boost revenue by requiring users to log in.
details: Reddit announced a major shift in its platform strategy: a transition to a primarily "logged-in experience." This move is a direct response to declining search traffic, partly due to the rise of AI-powered search engines that summarize information without requiring users to visit websites.

The company aims to protect its vast data from AI scraping, which has become a significant concern for publishers. By controlling access, Reddit hopes to forge lucrative licensing deals with AI model providers, turning its data into a revenue stream.

This change also comes as Reddit faces a decline in daily active users in its largest market, the U.S. While global daily active users remained flat at 130.3 million in Q3, U.S. users dropped to 50.7 million, a 2% year-over-year decrease. Search traffic referrals alone fell by over 1 million per week in October.

Despite user growth challenges, Reddit has shown strong monetization capabilities. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million in Q3, with advertising revenue up 54% to $847 million and non-advertising revenue (including AI data licensing) growing 35% to $48 million.

Logged-in users are more valuable to advertisers as they provide richer data signals for better ad targeting and personalization. This shift is expected to enhance Reddit's ability to monetize its audience, even as it navigates a changing web landscape.

CEO Steve Huffman acknowledged the significance of the change, calling it a "big evolution" but the "right decision for our platform and our business." He noted that the company will test the logged-in experience in select markets outside the U.S. in Q4 before a wider rollout, with no firm timeline yet established.
Reddit also emphasized that the shift does not mean an end to anonymity, as an "incognito mode" experience is being rebuilt, allowing for anonymous browsing even within a logged-in framework.

topic: report: chinese spy plot targeted nvidia ceo jensen huang
headline_marked: [[Chinese spy plot]] allegedly targeted Nvidia CEO, Trump ignored intel
headline: Chinese spy plot allegedly targeted Nvidia CEO, Trump ignored intel
summary: Report claims a Chinese citizen with ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been a spy, and that Donald Trump ignored intelligence on the matter.
details: US intelligence agencies reportedly investigated a Chinese spy plot that allegedly targeted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, a key AI advisor to former President Donald Trump.

According to sources speaking to The New York Times, Trump was briefed about a Chinese citizen, identified as Alice Huang (not related to Jensen Huang), who had direct access to the Nvidia CEO and may have been funneling secrets to China.

Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was suspected of helping China evade export controls for high-end Nvidia chips. Investigators were alarmed to find she might have leveraged her access to Jensen Huang to influence Trump's AI policy and feed intelligence to Beijing.
The report suggests that Trump chose not to act on the intelligence, partly out of concern that action against the alleged spying could harm Nvidia's stock or disrupt US-China trade relations.

Nvidia has denied that Alice Huang had access to any trade secrets. However, it is noted that Jensen Huang did not receive a defensive briefing typically given to targets of foreign spying, possibly because agencies feared he might tip off the suspect.
The Chinese Embassy in Washington has dismissed the US accusations as baseless, calling them "groundless smears and slanders."

The report also highlights Jensen Huang's influence on trade policy, suggesting his relationships have stalled investigations and proposed sanctions involving China or Nvidia within the Commerce Department.
